llm.summary: The skill bundle appears operational rather than malicious, but it gives an agent broad credential-backed power to change production tools, alerts, dashboards, Slack content, and ClawHub admin state.

dimensions.detail: Most capabilities match SRE, release, moderation, and Axiom management purposes, but the bundle includes generic raw API helpers and references for high-impact operations such as deleting Axiom datasets/tokens/users and mutating Slack messages, channels, files, and profiles.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Several high-impact ClawHub and dashboard workflows require dry runs, explicit targets, or confirmation, but generic Axiom and Slack API wrappers allow broad mutation methods without comparable built-in confirmation or narrow scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts are plain skill instructions and helper scripts under the skill tree; I found no hidden installer, obfuscated payload, or install-time autorun behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skills intentionally use local credentials from configuration files and contact Axiom, Grafana, Pyroscope, Sentry, Slack, GitHub, npm, and ClawHub services; this is expected for the stated operational purpose but should be limited to trusted workspaces.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The Axiom SRE skill creates local config and memory under the user's home directory, syncs configured org memory with git, and can auto-commit/push org memory entries; this is disclosed, but it persists incident knowledge outside the current repository.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only for agents and users trusted to operate production observability, Slack, release, and ClawHub admin workflows. Use least-privilege tokens, avoid configuring Slack or Axiom scopes the agent does not need, and require explicit human approval before any destructive API call, Slack mutation, production deploy, npm release, moderation action, or org-memory push.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector:clean] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues, so the Review verdict is based on artifact-backed authority scope rather than scanner labels.
[VirusTotal:clean] expected: VirusTotal reported no detections across the supplied engines; this supports absence of known malware but does not resolve the broad mutation-authority concern.
